A VPN is like a private tunnel between your phone or laptop and another computer somewhere else.

Normally, the websites you visit can see where you are, and your internet provider can see which sites you open. With a VPN, everything you send goes into the tunnel first, scrambled so nobody on the way can read it. It comes out at the other end, and that computer talks to the website for you.

So the website sees the VPN's location, not yours. It is handy on public Wi-Fi, or when you want more privacy from your internet provider. But the VPN company can see your traffic instead, so pick one you trust.
